summary: resolvePublic now decodes once inside try/catch, rejects NUL bytes and backslashes, resolves against an absolute public base and accepts only paths strictly inside it per path.relative; it returns null instead of escaping public/ or throwing.

tests.name: E2E-2: traversal and absolute request paths never leave public/
E2E-3: malformed percent-encoding returns null without throwing
F1: literal ../ traversal (reported case) returns null
F1: traversal nested deeper than its start still escapes and returns null
F1: percent-encoded traversal (upper/lower case, encoded slash) returns null
F1: sibling directory sharing the public prefix is rejected
F1: the public directory itself is not a file and returns null
F1: double-encoded traversal is decoded once and stays literal inside public/
F1: backslash paths (Windows-style input) return null
F1: absolute-looking request paths are rooted at public/, never the filesystem
F1: a relative root is resolved to an absolute public base
F2: lone % (reported case) returns null without throwing
F2: invalid hex escape returns null without throwing
F2: truncated or invalid UTF-8 sequence returns null without throwing
F2: non-string request paths return null without throwing

fixes.note: Resolve the request against path.resolve(root,'public') with the decoded path rooted at it, then accept only when path.relative(base,candidate) is non-empty, not '..', does not start with '..'+sep and is not absolute; reject NUL bytes and backslashes before resolving. The public dir itself returns null (not a file). Only src/serve.mjs maps request paths (git grep for decodeURI/path.join/resolve), so this is the one site.
fixes.rule: a path built from untrusted input is returned only after the final normalized filesystem path is proven (by path.relative, not string prefix) to lie strictly inside the absolute public base, and only from input the filesystem reads the same way the check does
